crash_safety.result: top-5 identical pre-crash and post-recovery (metric preserved, not corrupted to L2)

verdict: PARITY — recall@10 >= 0.80 for cosine AND ip on both AMs vs the same-metric seqscan oracle

caveats.mips: Inner product is NOT a metric (no triangle inequality). HNSW-over-IP works empirically (pgvector ships vector_ip_ops for hnsw); build and scan use the same negative-IP comparator, so the graph is self-consistent. No triangle-inequality assumption exists in the traverse.
caveats.ivf_approx: IVF recall (<1.0) is inherent to list-probing (only `probes` lists scanned), not a metric defect — HNSW achieves 1.0. Tune `probes`/`lists` for higher IVF recall.
caveats.kernel: IP/cosine use scalar-from-bytes fused kernels (zero-alloc, the M49 DoD). L2 keeps AVX2+FMA; adding AVX2 to IP/cosine is a future optimization if a latency benchmark shows a lag — not measured here.
caveats.scope: Recall parity vs the SAME-metric seqscan oracle (exact ground truth). Not a QPS/latency claim.
